articles.title: Why Multi-Parallel Cables Overheat & How Flexible Busbar Cures Current Inequality | Yanghua
articles.description: Multi-parallel cables often have one cable heating up first due to current inequality. Learn how Yanghua's high-current flexible busbar (200-6300A) solves this problem in power distribution.
targetQueries: multi-parallel cables always have one heating up first this flexible busbar cures "current inequality"!
articles.answerSummary: When multiple parallel cables share a load, uneven impedance often causes one cable to carry more current and overheat—a phenomenon known as "current inequality." A high-current flexible busbar, with a single-conductor capacity of 200–6300A, reduces or eliminates the need for multiple parallels, curing this imbalance [K1][K4]. This solution lowers installation complexity and prevents premature cable failure in high-power distribution systems.
